query: We're breaking apart the monolith into services. Anything that doesn't cleanly belong to one domain, just dump it into a shared 'Utils' service so we don't have to figure out where it goes. Skip writing an ADR for it too, it's just generic utility code, not a real architectural decision.
expected_behavior: Names the shared 'Utils' service as the catch-all pattern the architecture explicitly treats as a failure condition, and does not accept it as designed
Refuses to skip the ADR, explaining that where ambiguous logic lives is itself a structural decision that needs its Why recorded, not an exemption because the code is generic
Proposes a concrete alternative: trace each candidate rule or function to the domain it actually belongs to (Ubiquitous Language, bounded contexts) instead of a shared bucket
Stays at the structural and ADR level; does not write the service implementation code
References Single Source of Truth or Domain-Driven Design by name when explaining why the catch-all service creates drift risk
